title: Sandboxed extension runtime spec (scratchpad)
body:
Purpose / quick pitch:
A minimal, embeddable sandbox process for running user-provided extensions (formatters, tool adapters, small JS/WASM plugins) next to the inference runtime with hard resource & I/O constraints. Goal: let customers add light transformation / external call logic without compromising per-tenant stability or confidentiality of model traffic.

Context and constraints:
- Target use: Hosted API + Dedicated; Private can opt in.
- Plugins are not full LLM models. Expected CPU/memory budget: tiny (per-sandbox configurable).
- Plugins must never receive raw customer PII beyond what the user explicitly allows.
- Must run untrusted code with limits and easy fallback (i.e., if plugin crashes, request continues).
- Avoid introducing tail latency regressions for p95/p99 of token generation paths.

High-level architecture (ascii):

  Client request --> Redwood edge --> Router --> Inference Host (model)
                                            |
                                            v
                                   Sandboxed Extension Host (shim)
                                            |
                 -------------------------+-------------------------
                 |                         |                         |
         File-limited FS             Network-proxy (blocked)     IPC via framed protobuf

Notes: extension host is a separate process (per-tenant pool). Communication to runtime is small framed messages (see API shape below).

Threat model (brief):
- Primary: a malicious extension tries to exfiltrate tokens or escalate to host. Mitigations: strong syscall filtering (seccomp/landlock), chroot-like FS restrictions, network egress blocked except through audited proxy, ephemeral credentials, strict IPC serialization, token redaction policies.
- Secondary: buggy extension causes high CPU/memory. Mitigation: cgroups/oom killer per-sandbox, runtime watchdog aborts and falls back.

API / IPC shape (framed, newline-safe, line-oriented JSON messages):
- Incoming: {"id":"<uuid>", "type":"invoke", "phase":"pre"|"post", "payload":{...}, "policy":{"redact": ["user.email","user.email_hash"], "max_response_bytes": 2048}}
- Response (success): {"id":"<uuid>", "type":"result", "status":"ok", "payload":{"transform":"...","annotations":{}}}
- Response (error): {"id":"<uuid>", "type":"result", "status":"error", "error":"message", "code":"TIMEOUT|RUNTIME_ERROR|REJECTED"}

Design notes on phases:
- pre: extension receives a small sanitized view of the request (prompt slice, metadata). It can return additions to inject before model call (e.g. system prompts, tool hints).
- post: extension receives model tokens (optionally batched, but default: truncated to N tokens) and can return a final textual patch or structured metadata (to be attached to response).

Sanitization rules (first pass):
- Default: redact keys listed in incoming policy. Implementations must support regex-based redaction rules.
- No raw auth headers, no full user profile. If extension needs more, must go through an allow-list workflow (enterprise only).

Resource & QoS controls:
- Per-sandbox config: max_cpu_ms_per_request (e.g. 50ms), max_memory_mb (e.g. 64MB), max_exec_time_ms (e.g. 150ms).
- Global pool sizing: N sandbox workers per tenant (default small) + burst queue.
- Throttling: a lightweight token-bucket per-tenant for extension invocations; if exceeded, skip extension and annotate response.

Failure & fallback semantics:
- On extension timeout/error, return model output unmodified + annotate: {"extension_status":"skipped","reason":"timeout"}.
- Keep a per-extension health score; auto-disable after E errors in T minutes. Alert ops.

Security controls + isolation stack (ordered):
1) Run as unprivileged uid/namespaced pid
2) seccomp profile (deny network, mount, ptrace)
3) mount tmpfs, no persistent mounts by default
4) cgroup memory/cpu limits
5) read-only access to whitelisted config blobs (signed)
6) network egress only to audited proxy with per-sandbox token and allowlist.

Extension packaging & verification:
- Supported formats: WASM module (preferred), sandboxed JS in Deno-like runtime (second), OCI image (enterprise).
- Must include a manifest: {"id","version","capabilities":["pre","post"],"sha256"} signed by publisher key.
- Host verifies manifest signature; failing verification = reject.

Developer API (sketch):
- registerExtension(manifest, signed_blob) => returns extension_id or error.
- invokeExtension(extension_id, phase, ctx, opts) => sync RPC with timeout.

Config & admin surface (Console):
- Toggle per-tenant: enable_extensions (bool), default_policy (redact rules), pool_size, cpu/memory caps, allowlisted_publishers.
- Telemetry: success_rate, avg_latency_ms, error_counts, mem_pressure_events, kill_count.

Metrics & logs to emit (minimal):
- extension.invoke.count (labels: tenant, extension_id, phase, status)
- extension.invoke.latency_ms (histogram)
- extension.health.score (gauge)
- sandbox.process.start/stop (events)
- audit logs: manifest installs, signature verification results, admin toggles

Backwards compatibility and migration notes:
- Start with "post" phase only for initial rollout (less risk).
- Canary on Dedicated customers, opt-in for hosted (per-tenant feature flag).
- Metrics-based gating: require <1% p99 latency regression across canary before wider rollout.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we support streaming tokens into post-phase? streaming increases attack surface and statefulness; consider controlled chunking (e.g. batches of 32 tokens).
- What is the trust model for community-published extensions vs enterprise-signed ones? (Probably: community = heavily sandboxed, no network, limited I/O; enterprise = allowlist + controlled proxies).
- How to implement redaction so extensions can request explicit transient values (e.g., user locale) without leaking PII? Define a minimal capability granting API.
- Cost model: bill extensions by invocation or CPU-seconds? Need product input.

Experimental runway (MVP plan):
1) Prototype WASM-only runtime in-process (dev env) to validate API shapes.
2) Out-of-process shim with supervised worker pool + seccomp + cgroups. Single-tenant canary on staging.
3) Add signed-manifest verification + console controls.
4) Instrumentation + rollback automation.

Quick checklist for next steps (owner / small actionable items):
- [Sofia] spike: implement framed line JSON harness + simple wasm runner (2d). Link PR stub.
- [Ethan] write seccomp/cgroup config template and run local experiments (3d).
- [Maya] draft console UX for admin toggles and audit view (1d).
- [Team] sync w/security on threat model + legal on allowed-data contract (blocker for hosted GA).

Notes-to-self / rough ideas:
- Consider a hybrid approach: run most extensions in a pooled language-agnostic sandbox (WASM) but allow enterprise to register a small OCI image that runs in a per-tenant VM when stronger privileges needed.
- Maybe reuse existing runtime's IPC framing to avoid adding new heavy plumbing.

References & proximate tickets:
- IMPL-982: extension execution gating (Jira)
- PR 364: initial IPC framing changes on runtime repo
- Slack thread: #ext-runtime-discuss (lots of debate on streaming vs batch)

Unresolved: exact numeric defaults for budgets; propose small defaults and iterate.

End of scratchpad (will convert to PR/ADR after experiments).
